questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following enzymes is used as washing powders?

explanation.solution_text_en: Lipases (along with proteases) are active ingredients in biological washing detergents that break down greasy fat and oil stains on clothing.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Lipases break down oil and fat stains in laundry detergent powders.
explanation.key_concept: Industrial biotechnology: Enzyme applications in detergents.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing fruit-juice clarifying pectinase or cheese chymosin with detergents.

questions.question_text_en: What happens when the substrate molecule binds to the active site of an enzyme?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The substrate and the enzyme will bond permanently.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: They form a stable intermediate substance.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The amino acids in the active site become unreactive.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The chemical bonds of the substrate are distorted.

explanation.solution_text_en: Under the induced-fit model, binding to the active site induces conformational strain, distorting specific chemical bonds in the substrate and lowering the energy required for bond cleavage.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Binding distorts chemical bonds in the substrate, making them easier to break.
explanation.key_concept: Induced-fit catalytic mechanisms and transition state stabilization.
explanation.common_pitfall: Assuming substrate binding creates permanent irreversible bonds.

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following vitamins is used as a component of cofactor?

explanation.solution_text_en: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) forms the essential prosthetic coenzyme/cofactor building block for flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and flavin mononucleotide (FMN).
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) is the precursor for FAD cofactors in metabolism.
explanation.key_concept: Vitamins as coenzyme precursors in enzyme kinetics.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing water-soluble B2 cofactors with lipid-soluble vitamins.

questions.question_text_en: How does crossing over during meiosis bring variation in species?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Increasing the amount of genes in one of the parents during meiosis

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Combination of genes in the gametes that are not found in either parent

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Combining sex and somatic cell chromosomes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Creating genes that are not found in both parents due to meiosis

explanation.solution_text_en: Crossing over (chiasmata formation) between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I swaps genetic alleles, creating unique recombinant combinations of alleles in gametes.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Crossing over shuffles alleles to create novel gene combinations in gametes.
explanation.key_concept: Genetic recombination during meiotic crossing over.
explanation.common_pitfall: Claiming crossing over creates brand new genes from scratch.

questions.question_text_en: How does our body synthesize some of the amino acids in our body?

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: From intermediate molecules of different pathways

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: From the breakdown of pre-existing proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: From the biological breakdown of our own cells

explanation.solution_text_en: Non-essential amino acids are synthesized de novo by transamination of metabolic intermediates derived from glycolysis (e.g. pyruvate, 3-phosphoglycerate) and the Krebs cycle (oxaloacetate, alpha-ketoglutarate).
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Non-essential amino acids are made by converting intermediate molecules from glycolysis and Krebs cycle.
explanation.key_concept: Transamination and biosynthesis of non-essential amino acids.
explanation.common_pitfall: Believing our bodies synthesize amino acids from pure fatty acids.

questions.question_text_en:
This item is based on the following list of events during cloning of an insulin gene into plasmid:
I. Obtaining insulin-producing cells and plasmid from organisms
II. Cutting the insulin gene and plasmid
III. X
IV. Inserting the recombinant plasmid into bacteria
V. Production of insulin by bacteria
Which one of the following best represents the step listed as 'X'?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Inserting the insulin gene into a bacterium

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Inserting the open plasmid into a bacterium

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Fusing the insulin and plasmid genes to the cell wall of bacteria

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Combining the insulin gene into the opened plasmid

explanation.solution_text_en: After cutting both the human cDNA and bacterial plasmid with restriction endonucleases (step II), step III (X) is annealing and ligating the insulin gene into the opened plasmid vector using DNA ligase.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Step X is joining the cut insulin gene into the opened plasmid ring with DNA ligase.
explanation.key_concept: Recombinant DNA gene cloning workflow.
explanation.common_pitfall: Attempting transformation into bacteria before ligating the gene into the plasmid.

questions.question_text_en: Consider the DNA molecule containing: Strand 1: T A C G T A; Strand 2: A T G C A T. What will be the sequence of the new DNA if the DNA replicates semi-conservatively?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Original strand: ATGCAT; New strand: UACGUA

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Original strand: TACGTA; New strand: ATGCAU

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Original strand: ATGCAT; New strand: ATGCAT

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Original strand: TACGTA; New strand: ATGCAT

explanation.solution_text_en: In semiconservative replication, each parental strand acts as a template for synthesizing a complementary daughter strand using base-pairing rules (A-T, C-G). Original strand TACGTA pairs with newly synthesized ATGCAT.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Original template strand TACGTA directs synthesis of complementary DNA strand ATGCAT.
explanation.key_concept: Meselson-Stahl semiconservative DNA replication and base pairing.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing DNA replication with RNA transcription by inserting uracil (U).

questions.question_text_en: During translation, the

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: tRNA serves as a template of the DNA molecule.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: ribosome moves forward over two codons at a time.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: mRNA brings amino acids into the ribosomes.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: tRNA with complementary anticodon binds on the codon of mRNA.

explanation.solution_text_en: During translation elongation, aminoacyl-tRNA molecules carrying specific amino acids base-pair their complementary 3-base anticodon with mRNA codons in the ribosome A-site.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: tRNA anticodon matches and binds to the complementary mRNA codon during translation.
explanation.key_concept: Mechanism of translation on the ribosome.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing tRNA with mRNA or thinking ribosomes move two codons at a time.

questions.question_text_en: The step of the scientific method which comes after analyzing results and drawing a conclusion is

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Designing and carrying out an experiment.

explanation.solution_text_en: After analyzing experimental data and drawing logical conclusions, the investigator must determine whether the evidence supports accepting or rejecting the initial hypothesis.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Conclusions lead directly to accepting or rejecting the initial hypothesis.
explanation.key_concept: Steps of the scientific method and hypothesis evaluation.
explanation.common_pitfall: Choosing initial research steps that occur prior to experimentation.

questions.question_text_en: In a group of individuals in which Group A was a control and Group B was an experimental group, a student gave a placebo to the control group and an unknown drug to the experimental group. At the end, the experimental group got better. Which one of the following is true about the result?

explanation.solution_text_en: In a controlled trial, since the experimental group receiving the active drug showed significant health improvement compared to the inert placebo control, the evidence indicates the drug has a positive therapeutic effect.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: The experimental drug produced measurable recovery beyond the placebo baseline.
explanation.key_concept: Controlled scientific experimentation and placebo controls.
explanation.common_pitfall: Claiming no conclusion can be drawn from a statistically valid controlled trial.

questions.question_text_en: A biologist conducted a simple experiment to investigate the effect of pH on salivary amylase. She added 5cm3 amylase solution into 5cm3 starch suspension with a neutral pH in a test tube. After ten minutes, she tested it with iodine reagent and the solution turned into blue-black color. What is the dependent variable of this experiment?

explanation.solution_text_en: The independent variable is pH. The measured/observed response indicating whether starch was hydrolyzed or intact (rate of enzyme digestion) is the color change / formation of blue-black color.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: The measured outcome (blue-black color intensity) is the dependent variable.
explanation.key_concept: Identifying independent, dependent, and controlled variables in experiments.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing the manipulated parameter (pH) with the measured outcome variable.

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following pairs of biological tools and their functions is FALSE?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Petri dish - used for culturing microorganisms

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Quadrate - to separate solids from liquids

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Optical microscope - use beam of light to produce magnified image

explanation.solution_text_en: A quadrat (quadrate frame) is an ecological field tool used for quantitative sampling of plant and sessile organism population densities, not for liquid-solid filtration.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: A quadrat is used for sampling organism populations in ecology, not for filtering liquids.
explanation.key_concept: Laboratory and ecological field apparatus functions.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing ecological quadrats with laboratory filter funnels.

questions.question_text_en: Grade 12 students went to a field and collected plant specimens for identification in the laboratory. They wanted to preserve the plant parts for some time and specimens can be analyzed later. Which one of the following biological tools is used for their activities?

explanation.solution_text_en: A plant press uses wooden frames, absorbent blotting paper, and straps to flatten and dry botanical specimens for long-term herbarium preservation and taxonomic analysis.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: A plant press flattens and dries collected plant specimens for preservation.
explanation.key_concept: Botanical field preservation tools and herbarium methods.
explanation.common_pitfall: Selecting animal traps (pitfall) or survey theodolites for plant preservation.

questions.question_text_en: Some amino acids are synthesized using the transamination process in the cell. This activity more describes the cell's

explanation.solution_text_en: Anabolism refers to biosynthetic metabolic pathways that construct complex biomolecules (such as synthesizing amino acids and proteins) from simpler precursors, requiring energy.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Synthesizing new biomolecules like amino acids is anabolism (constructive metabolism).
explanation.key_concept: Metabolic classification: Anabolism (synthesis) vs Catabolism (breakdown).
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing constructive synthesis (anabolism) with destructive breakdown (catabolism).

questions.question_text_en: Identify the statement that correctly explains the factors of an enzyme activity.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Excessive heat breaks the ionic bonds that hold the tertiary structure of the enzyme protein.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Hydrogen ion concentration affects the ionic bonds of an enzyme.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Increasing concentration of substrates does not affect enzyme activity.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Inhibitors increase enzyme activity by increasing their turnover rate.

explanation.solution_text_en: Changes in pH (hydrogen ion [H+] concentration) alter the ionization state of acidic and basic amino acid R-groups, disrupting ionic bonds and salt bridges that maintain enzyme active site conformation.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: pH changes alter H+ concentration, disrupting ionic bonds in the enzyme.
explanation.key_concept: Physicochemical factors affecting enzyme kinetics: pH and ionic interactions.
explanation.common_pitfall: Attributing thermal denaturation primarily to ionic bonds rather than hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions.

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about allosteric regulation?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Enzymes are activated when activators attach to the active site.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Inhibition by competitive inhibitors occurs when they interact at the allosteric site.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Activation by activators occurs when they interact at the allosteric site.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Allosteric inhibition occurs when inhibitors attach to the active site.

explanation.solution_text_en: Allosteric regulation occurs when an effector molecule (activator or inhibitor) binds to an allosteric regulatory site distinct from the active site, inducing a conformational shift that alters catalytic activity.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Allosteric activators bind at allosteric regulatory sites away from the active site.
explanation.key_concept: Allosteric enzyme regulation and conformational kinetics.
explanation.common_pitfall: Confusing the allosteric site with the substrate-binding active site.

questions.question_text_en: If an enzyme from thermophilic bacteria, which catalyzes glucose 6-phosphate into fructose 6-phosphate in the process of glycolysis, is subjected to below the optimum temperature, the rate of the reaction will decrease. This is because

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The particles have more kinetic energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: More collisions between enzyme and glucose 6-phosphate occurred.

explanation.solution_text_en: Below optimum temperature, molecules have lower thermal kinetic energy, leading to fewer effective collisions between enzyme active sites and substrates, forming fewer enzyme-substrate complexes per second.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: Low temperatures decrease kinetic collisions, forming fewer enzyme-substrate complexes.
explanation.key_concept: Temperature dependence of enzyme kinetics (kinetic collision theory).
explanation.common_pitfall: Believing cold temperatures denature enzymes (cold slows kinetics; high heat denatures).

questions.question_text_en: Cyclooxygenase-2 is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins, which promote pain and fever in our body. The painkiller ibuprofen acts as a non-competitive inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-2, reducing the production of prostaglandins. What would happen if the concentration of ibuprofen increased?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Pain of the body is decreased.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Concentration of arachidonic acid is decreased.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Substrate affinity of cyclooxygenase-2 is higher.

explanation.solution_text_en: Increasing the concentration of ibuprofen (an inhibitor of COX-2) further suppresses prostaglandin synthesis, thereby reducing inflammatory fever and decreasing pain sensations in the body.
explanation.simpler_explanation_en: More ibuprofen blocks more COX-2, lowering prostaglandins and decreasing pain.
explanation.key_concept: Enzyme inhibition pharmacology: NSAIDs and pain mediation.
explanation.common_pitfall: Thinking higher inhibitor levels increase prostaglandin production.
